elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to an affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The notwithstanding carve-out expressly permits Customer to assign the Agreement to an affiliate, overriding the preceding consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor organization by merger without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The consent-free carve-out expressly covers a successor organization by merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor organization by acquisition without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The consent-free carve-out expressly covers a successor organization by acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor organization through a sale of substantially all assets without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The consent-free carve-out expressly includes a successor organization through a sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The added IBM provision requires Customer's prior written consent to any IBM assignment.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The IBM assignment provision expressly states that Customer's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause categorically states that IBM will not assign to a competitor of Customer.

elements.element: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that a change of control of Customer will not give IBM any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The notwithstanding carve-out permits assignment to a successor organization by the listed succession transactions without IBM consent.

elements.element: Customer must provide Vendor with written notice when assigning the Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor carve-out contains no written-notice obligation.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: IBM has no successor carve-out; every IBM assignment requires Customer's prior written consent, and assignments to Customer competitors are prohibited outright.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer with written notice when assigning the Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause requires prior written consent rather than establishing a successor-assignment right conditioned only on written notice.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to a successor require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Customer may also assign to an affiliate without IBM consent, even where that affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to Customer assignments requiring consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The general Customer assignment restriction requires IBM consent and expressly states that such consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than assignments to a successor require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Customer's prior written consent for every IBM assignment, although it additionally prohibits assignments to Customer competitors.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignments requiring consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The IBM assignment provision expressly states that Customer's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The operative redline meets every preferred requirement: it adds the requested Customer affiliate and successor carve-outs, restricts IBM assignments through a reasonable-consent standard and an absolute competitor prohibition, and eliminates any IBM termination right arising from Customer's change of control. It does not satisfy the fallback because neither party has the required mutual successor-assignment mechanism based on written notice, and Customer's affiliate carve-out is broader than the fallback's successor-only exception. The changes are confined to the requested assignment and change-of-control protections and do not contradict the retained assignment terms.
